title: Compass and Summit
premise: Salvage diver Wendell Lockridge recovers a brass compass from a wreck the navy has quietly written off, and when an extreme low tide exposes a sea cave on the headland, he finds a skeleton clutching its twin — proof that his grandfather's lost 1948 expedition reached the summit cave and never came down. A well-funded consortium arrives with expiring concession permits, hiring Wendell as their guide while secretly hunting the expedition's mineral survey, which could make or break the region's future. As the ascent strips away supplies, trust, and two lives, Wendell discovers the consortium's lead backer is the navy officer who abandoned his grandfather on the mountain decades ago. In the end, Wendell chooses to burn the survey rather than let it be weaponized, brings home the survivors under cover of a storm, and lets the mountain keep its secret — inheriting not his grandfather's discovery, but his silence.
about_author: Edmund Zhou is a former commercial diver who spent six years working salvage contracts in the North Atlantic before turning to writing full-time. His fiction draws on the drowned places and hard bargains of coastal working towns, and 'Compass and Summit' is his third novel.

chapters.title: The Wreck They Won't Name
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Diving a restricted wreck site, Wendell salvages a brass compass stamped with his own family name, then lies to the navy liaison about finding it. The beat is quiet unease: a man who makes his living off other people's losses realizing one loss might be his own.

chapters.title: What the Low Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. An unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave below the cliffs; inside, a preserved skeleton grips an identical compass and a rotted survey case marked 1948. Emotional beat: grief and vertigo as family legend becomes physical fact, and Wendell pockets the survey before anyone else can see it.

chapters.title: Men With Permits
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The consortium arrives — charming project lead Imogen Vale, ex-military security chief Dray, and a geologist who asks too-specific questions about the headland. They offer Wendell triple rate to guide an 'environmental survey.' Beat: temptation sharpened by suspicion; Wendell accepts, telling himself knowledge is leverage.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, interwoven with 1948 letters from his grandfather Elias. The letters reveal the expedition found something in the summit cave worth killing for, and that Elias trusted one man above all: a young naval officer named Corrick. Beat: dread of recognition — Corrick's name appears on the consortium's funding paperwork.

chapters.title: The Approach
chapters.summary: Alternating Wendell and geologist Mara Okonkwo POVs. The team hikes toward the high country as weather windows narrow; Dray tests Wendell's loyalty with a veiled threat about his diving licenses. Beat: rising pressure and fragile camaraderie; Mara privately suspects the survey's true purpose and shares a fragment of it with Wendell.

chapters.title: Whiteout at the Col
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A storm traps the team at a col; a rope team error nearly kills a porter, saved only by Wendell's ice skills. Supplies are destroyed. Beat: survival's true price made literal — the mountain takes its tax, and Dray begins rationing trust along with food.

chapters.title: The Cave That Charges Admission
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They reach the summit cave and find Elias's camp, a final journal, and the mother lode the survey maps: a rare-earth deposit vast enough to remake the coast — or strip-mine it. Dray reveals orders to secure it by any means. Beat: awe curdling into horror; Wendell realizes why the navy wrote off the wreck.

chapters.title: Corrick's Confession
chapters.summary: Dray's POV, then Wendell's. The aged Corrick arrives by helicopter, confessing he abandoned Elias in 1948 on orders, and offers Wendell wealth and erasure in exchange for the survey. When Wendell refuses, Dray moves to take it by force. Beat: betrayal crystallized; power showing exactly what it buys.

chapters.title: Descent in the Storm
chapters.summary: Wendell and Mara's POV. Wendell burns the survey pages in the cave stove, triggering a violent scramble down the mountain through the storm; Dray falls to his death pursuing them, and Corrick, broken, stays behind at Elias's camp by choice. Beat: climax — Wendell pays the inheritance's price, choosing silence over fortune.

chapters.title: Compass and Summit
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The surviving team reports a failed environmental survey; permits expire unclaimed. Wendell returns the second compass to the sea above the cave, keeping only Elias's letter, and tells Imogen — who suspected all along and says nothing — that some wrecks should stay sunk. Beat: bittersweet resolution; inheritance redefined as the courage to refuse what you're owed.
